bib.title: Chapter 7: Creating and Connecting a Knowledge Graph to an AI Agent (Building AI Agents with LLMs, RAG, and Knowledge Graphs)

question: How can knowledge graphs be built with an LLM, connected to an LLM as retrieval context (GraphRAG), and reasoned over by LLMs, GNNs and KG embeddings?
contributions: Overview of KG fundamentals, taxonomies and ontologies
Five-stage KG construction pipeline with an LLM, plus a LangChain/Neo4j tutorial (custom prompt and LLMGraphTransformer)
GraphRAG framework (G-indexing, G-retrieval, G-generation), retrieval granularity and graph-to-prompt formats, applications
Introduction to KG embeddings, GNNs and LLM graph reasoning, and open challenges

results.claim: A KG is a directed graph of factual triplets (head, relation, tail), for example (Napoleon, BornIn, Ajaccio).

limits: Chapter is a survey-style overview with no experiments of its own; every performance statement is qualitative or cited from other work.
Tutorial code is shown only in part; the full code is in the Packt GitHub repo. The LLM, Neo4j version and LangChain version are not stated in the chapter.
Code uses langchain.chains.GraphCypherQAChain and langchain_experimental LLMGraphTransformer, since moved or flagged in later LangChain versions.
KG embeddings and GNNs are explicitly out of scope beyond an introduction.
The GoT worked example mixes miles and km.
practices: Define the KG's purpose with stakeholders first, then ontologies, top-down or bottom-up, reusing existing domain ontologies for interoperability (Knowledge creation).
Build a KG through five stages: creation, assessment, cleaning, enrichment, deployment; assessment and cleaning can run together (Creating a KG).
For custom LLM triplet extraction, write a prompt with a task bullet list (do and do not), role context, and few-shot examples (Creating a KG with an LLM).
Use LLMGraphTransformer from LangChain for a few-line structured extraction (Creating a KG with an LLM).
Use one LLM to extract and a smaller LLM to correct (Knowledge creation).
Assess a KG on accuracy, completeness, conciseness (watch blank nodes), timeliness, accessibility, understandability, security/privacy/traceability (Knowledge assessment).
Use an LLM to detect erroneous triplets such as (Vienna, CapitalOf, Hungary) (Knowledge cleaning).
Choose the KG store by use: relational, document, graph database (Neo4j/Cypher), or triplet store, or a hybrid or KG layer on top (Knowledge hosting).
Keep pipelines for knowledge updates, quality monitoring, deletion for legal/privacy reasons, and access control after deployment (Knowledge hosting).
Control GraphRAG granularity by retrieving nodes, triplets, paths, subgraphs or an adaptive mix; avoid saturating the context (Graph-guided retrieval).
Convert retrieved graphs to graph formats, natural language, syntax trees or code-like forms (GraphML) before prompting (Graph-enhanced generation).
Consider combining vector RAG and GraphRAG with a router (HybridRAG) (GraphRAG applications).
